stories.text: When the House of Lords threw out the Second Reform Bill on 8 October 1831, rioting broke out in Nottingham and a crowd burned the castle, which belonged to the Duke of Newcastle, an opponent of reform. Three men were hanged; the Duke refused to restore the castle, and its burnt shell stood on the rock for years.
The medieval castle was demolished after the Civil War and a ducal mansion built on the rock. Rioters burnt the mansion in 1831; it reopened as a museum in 1878.
Kate Watson Wallis (1852–1918), a suffragist, lived in the Residence at the Castle with her husband, the Castle Art Gallery's first curator.
Sherwood Foresters Regimental Museum opened in 1923. Subject: war and conflict: regiment.
